notes.title: The issue regarding the DMCA claim has been resolved.
notes.content:
(For context regarding the DMCA action, please refer to our previous post.)

After the DMCA claim was filed, we reached out to inquire which part of The Game of Sisyphus allegedly used the music without permission. The DMCA responded to our request and forwarded our inquiry to the claimant.

As a result, the DMCA action has been temporarily suspended while waiting for a response from the claimant. However, since our game does not include any unauthorized use of music, and we suspect the claim was not made by the original copyright holder, it is unlikely that the claimant will respond.

We anticipate that the suspension will remain in effect indefinitely.

We would like to express our gratitude to all the players who have shown concern for our situation.

We do not use any music, art, or code without proper authorization, and we will continue to maintain a strong commitment to copyright compliance while developing quality games in the future.

The Game of Sisyphus will continue to be sold as normal.

notes.title: The Game of Sisyphus has received a DMCA notice.
notes.content:
Hello, dear players of The Game of Sisyphus.

We recently received a DMCA copyright complaint claiming that we used a specific audio track without authorization. 
(Due to potential legal issues, we will not disclose the details of the audio track at this time, but we may reveal it if the situation escalates.)

[h3]However, we want to clarify that The Game of Sisyphus does not contain the mentioned audio track.[/h3] 
We have not found any music in the game that could be considered similar to the alleged track. 
We believe this DMCA notice was submitted by mistake, and we are currently addressing the issue. 
Unfortunately, DMCA has only given us one day to respond, which means there is a possibility that our Steam store page may be taken down.

At The Game of Sisyphus, we respect the copyrights of all artists. 
All music in the game was either legally purchased or composed by our team’s composer. None of the music in the game was generated by AI.

We will provide the sources of all the music used in our game below for transparency.

notes.title: About the direction of the game
notes.content:
As many reviews have pointed out, our game fails to fulfill the role of a Foddian game. It has many drawbacks compared to Foddian games. Even if you become skilled at the game, fast gameplay is not possible. It doesn't provide a challenge to skilled players.

Our game is more of a Sisyphus experience game rather than a Foddian game.

Therefore, we have changed the store description to clearly define the identity of the game.

However, this does not mean that patches for hardcore gamers will stop.

We lacked a lot of understanding about the game.

We apologize to those who were disappointed with the game.

This message has been translated using a translation tool. There is no aggressive intent behind it.

notes.title: Difficulty Increase Notice
notes.content:
Difficulty Increase Notice

Due to a previous patch that lowered the difficulty, some segments became too easy. Instead of altering the core mechanics, we've decided to raise the obstacle difficulty. While there haven't been significant changes, the overall difficulty remains easier compared to before April 12th.

[list]
[*] Increased difficulty in intermittent cliff segments
[*] Raised difficulty in reconfigured segments
[*] Removal of some obstacles in ice segments
[*] Fix for sliding bug on ice bridges
[*] Fine-tuning of Oak Tree segment
[*] Introduction of new obstacles in bamboo segments
[*] Minor adjustments in other segments
[/list]

Difficulty increase in the mid-to-late game
Although we've increased the difficulty in some segments, it's not our intention to make every segment challenging. Our goal is to create a game that most people can clear with time investment. Some segments are designed to be easy when rolling down or ascending quickly.

The game is not challenging yet. We need your opinion on this.

However, there are concerns about the mid-game difficulty being too easy. We will actively consider and incorporate user feedback. Please leave your comments below. Thank you.

[*] Developer's comment:
[*] Sapphire Ball has been added for users seeking faster gameplay. It is currently in beta testing and has a lower difficulty level than anticipated. Moving the ball faster than Sisyphus caused several issues. If the ball moves too fast, it becomes challenging to control, leading to difficulties in character interaction. We believe this game is not like "Getting over it" or "A difficult game about Climbing," where an experienced player can clear the game in a short time. Gameplay time doesn't significantly differ between beginners and experts. We apologize to players who were not satisfied with the game. We'll strive to solve as many issues as possible and improve both the Sapphire Ball and the game in the future. Currently, it's not recommended for speedrunning. Please leave your comments below the post. We'll try new ideas and respond to them. Thank you.

notes.title: News for Speedrunners!
notes.content:
Hello speedrunners from around the world!

This is the development team of "The Game of Sisyphus".

I'd like to inform you in advance about the upcoming update for our game, as it has not been received well by the speedrunning community. Initially, our game was conceived as a simple meme game. However, due to its very slow mechanics, it has been pointed out as a drawback for speedrunning.
Therefore, we are currently planning and developing a new update specifically tailored for speedrunners.

Here's what we have in mind:

We will create a ball that can move very fast but is very difficult to control. Even a slight deviation to the left or right can make it fall, but it must move very quickly. It may be too challenging for casual gamers to play.

However, please note that this is currently in the planning stage, and there are many issues that need to be addressed. 
The current map is also not suitable for speedrunning. 
It will take several days for the update to be implemented. 
The development team's lack of expertise in speedrunning may result in insufficient testing.
Nevertheless, the ball designed for speedrunners will be available to play from the beginning without the need for purchase. 
If you are not satisfied, you can request a refund without extending your playtime.

Once the update is complete, an announcement will be made on Steam.

With respect to speedrunners,

(Translated into Google Translate)

notes.title: Update
notes.content: We advise against settings that exceed HD and 60FPS on the game loading screen. Setting the quality to 4K 120FPS and similar high-quality configurations may lead to issues even on high-spec computers during prolonged gameplay. The optimal settings are a resolution of 1920x1080 and a frame rate of 60FPS. Apologies if anyone else is having trouble playing with these high quality settings.

notes.title: Balance Update
notes.content:
Hello, we are the development team behind "The Game of Sisyphus."

With this update, the difficulty has slightly increased. 
The balance update includes the following changes:

[list]
[*] Some overly challenging sections have been slightly adjusted.
[*] The force of boulders falling downward has slightly increased.
[*] The strength to hold boulders manually has slightly decreased.
[/list]

Since the release, some players found the default gameplay too difficult to progress. 
Therefore, we significantly lowered the difficulty level (Update 4/12). 
However, this update inadvertently made sections with uneven floors too easy and almost non-functional as intended. 
Additionally, the slowed speed of falling boulders led to too many instances where boulders were stopped safely. 
To address these issues, we conducted this update.
With this update, the difficulty has increased by approximately 20% from the previous downward adjustment level.
However, please do not worry as the increase in difficulty is not significant.

Our goal is to make our game accessible to most players.
While Rage Games that require over 20 hours of play might be entertaining for streaming, we aim to create a game where anyone can feel a sense of accomplishment with just time and patience. 
For skilled players, challenging yourself with heavier and harder-to-control balls like Iron ball, Bronze ball, etc., can be rewarding.

Thank you, and we will support you in your journey.

notes.title: Guidelines
notes.content:
This is a guide for those who are struggling in the early stages of the game.

[olist]
[*] Approach the ball closely and then move slowly. If the ball tends to fall in an unwanted direction, press and hold the left or right mouse buttons to roll the ball sideways. Additionally, pressing the left or right movement keys to support the center of the ball is the key point.

[*] It's dangerous to let go of the ball. Jumping while rolling the ball is not a good choice.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44948270/2d91fe99ad9092c1b80ac9e86491754bb64cb861.gif[/img]

[*] Slowly rolling the ball to one side allows you to move laterally.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44948270/603164587e1ab47aec196adeccfa6d24f5e3c877.gif[/img]

[*] In sharp curves, try moving slowly without pressing the shift key.

[*] The game autosaves. If you're too tired, pause and then exit the game.

[*] If it's still too hard, try using the Beachball. It's a bit lighter and easier to control.
[/olist]
